changes: Persons, date and chronogram confirmed: rasa(6)-muni(7)-muni(7)-candra(1), read right to left = Śaka 1776, about 1854 CE; asita = kṛṣṇa pakṣa; vinikhati(!) = vilikhati, so Bhuvanānanda is the scribe.
Notes: the first reading stated that an intercalary Āṣāḍha 'indeed occurred in 1854'. This has not been checked, so it is now marked as unverified.
Notes: 'jinajo' is explained as possibly 'son of Jina', which would be a patronymic, or a corruption. No separate person is created for it.

notes: The chronogram rasa(6)-muni(7)-muni(7)-candra(1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1776. Āṣāḍha of that year falls in 1854 CE. 'vārddhy-āṣāḍha' most likely stands for vṛddhi-Āṣāḍha, the intercalary (adhika) month. Whether Śaka 1776 actually had an adhika Āṣāḍha has not been checked against an ephemeris. 'asita' means the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa pakṣa). 'vinikhati(!)' is a corruption of 'vilikhati'. 'jinajo' qualifies Bhuvanānanda and is unclear: it may mean 'son of Jina' (a patronymic, though the father's name would then be uncertain) or be a corruption, for example of 'dvijajo'. No separate person has been created for it. 'śrībadaryyākhya(!)' refers to the Badarī-māhātmya. This agrees with the catalogue fields (scribe Bhuvanānanda, Śāke 1776).
